drivers.evidence: Past closures show median 0.78x demand in the following week (noise-adjusted x0.78); 2 instances. This week has closure on Monday, reducing 1/5 of the week.

adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 140.8. Store closure on Monday (Halloween week) reduces demand; historical data shows a 22% drop in the week after a closure (noise-adjusted). Halloween has a weak historical lift (median x1.04, noise-adjusted x1.0). No promotion or price change. The classical uplift model's x1.00 is correct for Halloween, but the closure is a known demand reducer not in the model. Adjust down for closure only. Evidence is moderate (2 past closures), so shrink toward 1.0. No other drivers.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-37% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
